svg.aria-label: B2-F03 — POST-HOC: crossover arrives early, certifiable evidence arrives much later
svg.desc: Horizontal interval chart on a logarithmic time axis, one row per storage level. Each row starts at a small circle marking the crossover time and ends at a diamond marking the first record length at which the frozen selector certifies a window. At C_D = 100 the crossover is at 0.022 hours and certification first occurs at 32 hours, about 1.3 days. At C_D = 1000 the crossover is 0.25 hours and certification needs 398 hours, about 17 days. At C_D = 3000 it is 0.81 hours against 1259 hours, about 52 days. At C_D = 10000 it is 2.90 hours against 4467 hours, about 190 days. A vertical dashed rule at 48 hours marks the record length B2 actually ran, which falls short of every diamond except the first. The gap between circle and diamond spans two to three orders of magnitude in time.
